summary: The Archipelago Council: three sun-sea islands under a Tide-Speaker, home of the best white ships of the Sunhot fleets and the sayings of the islands.

tide_speaker.name: The Tide-Speaker
tide_speaker.desc: Hengara speaks for the three isles in the council hall above the harbour, and her voice is heard over the sound of the surf. She is chosen by the isle-councils, who count their votes in shells.

tide_charter.name: The Tide Charter
tide_charter.desc: The charter of the isles is written on a long scroll of palm-leaf and renewed at every spring tide. It binds the three islands as a net binds a catch.

sun_sea_masters.name: Masters of the Sun-Sea
sun_sea_masters.desc: Hengyang's captains have sailed the sun-sea since before the charts, and their white ships are the pride of every Sunhot fleet. A captain of the isles is never lost in his own water.

the_saying_of_the_isles.title: The Saying of the Isles
the_saying_of_the_isles.desc: Island traders bring a tale nobody can explain and say it must go to Gala. Their saying is older than the harbour: when the tales of men grow too old for any man to explain, carry them to Gala.

focuses.name: The Archipelago Council
focuses.desc: Hengyang is the northern archipelago of the Lands of the Sun, three island states governed by a council of the isles under a Tide-Speaker. Its white ships are the best of the Sunhot fleets.

focuses.name: The Tide-Speaker
focuses.desc: Hengara is the Tide-Speaker of the three isles, chosen by the council for her calm voice. She hears every dispute from a bench on the harbour wall.

focuses.name: The Three Isles
focuses.desc: Ferries ply between the three isles on a fixed timetable, and the quays are rebuilt in white stone. A traveller can reach any isle in a single tide.

focuses.name: The Isle Councils
focuses.desc: Each isle keeps a council of its own, with a bench for each village. The councils send delegates to the archipelago hall and keep the rest at home.

focuses.name: Voices of the Tides
focuses.desc: The council sends speakers to every Sunhot court, each with a shell and a message. A shell is a good gift: it carries the sound of the sea home with it.

focuses.name: The Tide Charter
focuses.desc: The charter is written out afresh on a roll of palm-leaf and sung in the council hall at the spring tide. Every islander knows its first verse.

focuses.name: The Sun-Sea Fleets
focuses.desc: Hengyang's yards are among the busiest in the south, and the white hulls slide into the water in a never-ending line. The shipwrights sing as they work.

focuses.name: Elven Hulls of Hengyang
focuses.desc: The elven hulls of the isles are long, narrow and swift, built of pale timber and rowed by crews of forty. A well-built hull outlasts three captains.

focuses.name: Harbour of the Three Isles
focuses.desc: A great harbour opens between the isles, protected by two moles and a chain of white towers. Every ship that passes must be seen from three sides.

focuses.name: The White Fleet
focuses.desc: Hengyang's war-hulls are painted white from keel to masthead, so that they can be seen from shore. Few fleets are as proud, and fewer as well drilled.

focuses.name: Steersmen of the Sun-Sea
focuses.desc: Steersmen of the isles guide ships through the shoals, reading the water by colour and the wind by sound. The harbour pays them well, and they spend it on shell-work.

focuses.name: Masters of the Sun-Sea
focuses.desc: The fleet's captains have charted every reef and eddy of the sun-sea, and their word is law on its waters. Ships from every realm give way.

focuses.name: Ships With the League
focuses.desc: The Noon League stands, and Hengyang's fleet puts to sea beneath its banner. The white hulls sail in line, and the sea gives way to them.

focuses.name: Sea Roads to the Isles
focuses.desc: Hengyang's traders sail the sea roads to the Islands of the South, with grain, cloth and glass. They return with news, spice and the islanders' sayings.

focuses.name: Trade With the Southern Isles
focuses.desc: The southern isles sell shell, salt and fish, and buy grain and tools in return. The merchants learn each other's weights and tongues, and the prices stay fair.

focuses.name: Tales From the Isles
focuses.desc: Tales from the southern isles are gathered by Hengyang's scribes and copied into a great archive. Some are songs, some are sailing lore, and some are simply old.

focuses.name: The Saying of the Isles
focuses.desc: The islanders say that when the tales of men grow too old for any man to explain, they must be carried to Gala. The council wonders what the saying means.

focuses.name: A Harbour for Strangers
focuses.desc: A guest-harbour is built on the southern shore of the greatest isle, with a lamp that is never put out and a hall that is never shut. Hengyang offers shelter to any ship that asks for it.
